core_obligations: Reformulate as torsion (proof lines 1958-1972): the long exact sequence of the sequence given by multiplication by a on the structure sheaf identifies the cokernel in question with the elements of the first cohomology annihilated by a; consequently the modules increase with the element, and boundedness for one element implies boundedness for its powers by the displayed exact sequence, so it suffices to find an element whose powers are divisible by the given one and for which the bound holds.
Reduce to a reduced quotient (proof lines 1972-1976): by the algebra lemma one may replace the given element by such an element with the additional property that the quotient ring is reduced.

Bound by the normalization of the quotient (proof lines 1978-2000): let B be the normalization of the quotient ring in its total quotient ring; since the base is Nagata the cokernel of the inclusion is finite, and its length is the bound; for a modification with normal source the scheme theoretic closure of the part of the divisor away from the exceptional locus is finite over the quotient ring by the finiteness in codimension one, hence is the spectrum of an intermediate ring between the quotient and its normalization; the restriction map on the sections of the divisor to those of the closure is injective, because a section in the kernel vanishes on the punctured locus, so by the injectivity lemma it comes from an element of the base ring which maps to zero in the intermediate ring, forcing the section to vanish.

Conclude (proof lines 2000-2004): hence the torsion module is a subquotient of the quotient of the intermediate ring by the base ring, and therefore its length is bounded by the length of the cokernel of the inclusion of the quotient ring into its normalization, uniformly in the modification.
proof_roadmap: Identify the cokernel with the torsion of the first cohomology and reduce to a convenient element whose powers dominate the given one.
Assume the quotient by that element is reduced and take its normalization, whose cokernel is finite by the Nagata assumption.
Show the torsion module is a subquotient of that finite cokernel by comparing with the scheme theoretic closure of the divisor and using the injectivity of the restriction map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a nonzero element of a two dimensional local normal Nagata domain there is an integer bounding the length of the cokernel of the restriction map from the base ring to the sections of the divisor cut out by that element along every normal modification (statement lines 1946-1956). The proof (proof lines 1958-2005) identifies that cokernel with the torsion of the first cohomology, reduces to an element with reduced quotient, compares with the normalization of the quotient and with the scheme theoretic closure of the divisor, and uses the injectivity of the restriction map to bound the torsion uniformly. H3: a reduction with a comparison argument, written out in full.
